newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open little changed.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open little changed.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open little changed Tuesday as traders expect the market to consolidate last week's sharp gains, traders said.

"It was basically a sideways trading day yesterday and we expect the market stabilize further," said one trader, who added the market still may run into some technical selling. "It looks overbought on the charts," he said.

Monday, New York cocoa futures ended flat to weaker, but speculative buying lifted prices off session lows. September ended down $3 $1,629 a tonne after ranging from $1,635 to $1,614. Spot July ended $11 lower at $1,581, while the back months finished unchanged to $3 weaker.
Technically, September cocoa was likely to find near-term support at $1,614-$1,611, traders said. They pegged July resistance at $1,635, followed by September's life-of-contract high of $1,644.
In London, cocoa futures were firmer early Tuesday, buoyed by trade buying. LIFFE September was up five stg at the midday break, to 1,128 stg, while spot July climbed eight stg, to 1,114 stg.
